subject: BJ's Wholesale Club Fuel Storage Remand Hearing
overview: The Council held a court-ordered remand hearing regarding a fuel storage license for BJ’s Wholesale Club and debated a special permit for Starbucks hours amidst labor concerns. The meeting also addressed municipal maintenance issues, ARPA funding for affordable housing, and environmental litter regulations.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognition and Minutes
items.summary: The Council recognized the Lunar New Year and approved the meeting records from January 10, 2023.

items.title: BJ's Wholesale Club Fuel Storage License Remand Hearing
items.summary: The Council conducted a remand hearing for a flammable storage license at 278 Middlesex Avenue, reviewing proposed site improvements including traffic queuing plans, electric vehicle chargers, and enhanced landscaping for neighboring residents. The hearing was kept open until January 31 to allow for further public comment and the formalization of permit conditions.

items.title: Starbucks Extended Hours Special Permit
items.summary: Tabled a request for extended hours at the College Avenue Starbucks until January 31 to obtain legal counsel regarding the Council's authority to consider labor disputes in permit decisions.

items.title: DCR Maintenance and Fellsway Construction
items.summary: Requested that the Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) provide a restoration plan for landscaping and sidewalks on the Fellsway.

items.title: Community Event Sites and Accessibility
items.summary: Requested the administration identify additional sites for city-sponsored events to increase neighborhood engagement and equity.

items.title: Sharps Disposal Access
items.summary: Requested the city improve accessibility and public communication regarding safe disposal sites for medical sharps.

items.title: Regulation of Miniature Liquor Bottles
items.summary: Referred a resolution to reduce 'nip' bottle litter through potential bans or fee implementations to the Economic Development Committee.

items.title: ARPA Funding for Affordable Housing
items.summary: Received a communication regarding the allocation of $400,000 in ARPA funds for permit fees related to the Medford Housing Authority project at 121 Riverside Avenue. Councilors criticized the administration's piecemeal approach to ARPA spending and requested a comprehensive financial report.
